title: POST /v1/action/propose request
description: Runner to compliance-server. Two forms: start a proposal ({start}) or poll it ({ticket}). The repository is the one of the OIDC token, never a body field. documents only travels with propose-with-model. Rules JSON Schema cannot state: in every fact line_end >= line_start; in every document bytes is the UTF-8 length of text and sha256 its SHA-256; document paths are unique; the bytes of all documents add up to at most 262144 (256 KiB).

version.description: Version of the reader contract. A new version is a new contract: every party moves together.

ticket.description: Opaque handle the 202 answer gave; bound to the repository of the token that started it.

categories.description: The attestable categories whose obligations the push left not_documented.

scan.description: The vulnerability scan of the same push, reduced to counts and a hash: the runner computes it over the reduced Trivy report it sent in the push; same trust as the push. finding_count is the number of findings, scanned_packages the number of packages the scan covered (zero findings over zero packages proves nothing), report_sha256 the SHA-256 of that reduced report. Absent when the push carried no scan. Only the field market_availability.no_known_exploitable_vulnerabilities of monitoring_lifecycle_report reads it.

category.description: The ten attestable categories: one template each in crates/compliance/attestations/templates/.

document.description: A text document of fixed name, whole, as it is in the tree of GITHUB_SHA.

model_document_path.description: Closed list of exact names the model may read: text documents only, no globs, never source code, workflows, dependabot.yml, lockfiles or CHANGELOG.md (those are read by the detectors, in the runner). Lowercase security.md is not listed: GitHub recognises SECURITY.md; whether it also recognises the lowercase name is not verified.

detector_id.description: Closed catalogue of detectors (plan R4 section 1, layer D, plus the hints the plan names). The step and the workflow of seetrex-ai/compliance-action itself are never a fact. security_contact is a reporting contact a third party can reach: an e-mail address, the Contact: of .well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116), or a URL outside the pushing repository; the .../security/advisories/new form of the pushing repository itself is never a security_contact fact, because the experiment treats every repository as private and a third party cannot open that form in a private repository.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes: no leading slash, no empty, '.' or '..' segment.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256. Validators in Python must use re.fullmatch (or \Z): with re.match or re.search, $ also accepts a trailing newline.
